title: Source registry file: starting URLs per brand (leads, not evidence), with an optional profile of how its pages state support

kind.description: How the pages state support: per_model_dates (a date per model), eol_list (a list of end-of-life models), years_after_eol (N years after a model's end of life), unknown (not read yet), lead_only (not the maker's own page; find its statement).

date_order.description: How these pages write numeric dates: dmy (31/12/2027) or mdy (12/31/2027). npm run validate reads numeric dates in quotes from evidence URLs starting with one of these URLs in this order only.

last_checked.description: Date the data refresh last fetched these URLs; null means never.

regions_by_url.description: Profile: the region codes each page covers, by its exact URL. Rule R2 rejects a record whose regions go beyond what the pages it cites cover together; a page not listed here covers none.

at_least.description: Profile: the sentences, or shorter phrases, that make this source's dates a minimum, written as the page text reads them; rule R3 compares them after normalise(), as the verifier compares quotes. R3 rejects an at_least: true record that quotes none of them, so an empty list means no record of this source may be at_least: true.

conditions.description: Profile: the conditions sentences allowed on a record that cites each URL. {version} stands for the hardware version exactly as the cited row writes it. Rule R4 requires a record citing a listed URL to carry one of its sentences, and rejects any other wording.

notes.description: Profile: the sentences a parser may write in notes for a record that cites each URL, in the order it joins them; a {name} placeholder stands for a value read from the row. No rule checks notes.

category_map.description: Profile: an ordered list of patterns to categories. The first entry whose model pattern matches the record's model, or whose row pattern matches one of its evidence quotes, gives the category; patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions. Rule R7 rejects a record whose category differs, or that no entry matches, unless category_exceptions lists it.

category_exceptions.description: Profile: record ids whose category is a hand judgement (for example from the maker's product page), with that category. Rule R7 checks these records against it instead of category_map.

versioned.description: Profile: true when the pages list each model by hardware version. Rule R6 then requires the model or the conditions, and every alias, to carry a version that a cited row writes, so a name can't match other versions of the model.

min_rows.description: Profile: the fewest rows a parser must find on each page before it trusts its read (B3's sanity gate), set at 90% of the rows the records cited when the profile was written.

renames.description: Profile: the maker's rename table, hand-kept from its pages: each old name, the new name it became, and the pages that state the change. Rule R1 accepts an alias that this table renames to the record's model; a parser maps a page's old name to the record.

parser_exceptions.description: Profile: record ids a parser must not write to, because a field carries a judgement no rule derives (a D33 split, a D39 conflict, a category or note from another page). A parser reports a changed row for them instead of proposing the record.
